text:
liam: Hi team, new hire here. Just got my MacBook Air (M2, shipped with macOS 13.5). MDM profile installed but when I try to sign into Slack or Google via SSO it says 'certificate pin mismatch' and the browser shows a weird org cert (looks like a proxy). Any pointers?

it-support: Welcome @liam! That error usually means the device sees a TLS interception device or our cert rotation didn't push correctly. Quick questions: are you on office Wi-Fi or personal hotspot? Do you see any captive portal or proxy in Settings -> Network?

liam: On redwood-secure, no captive portal. I tested with my phone hotspot and SSO worked there. On corp Wi-Fi the browser shows "redwood-corp-proxy" in the TLS chain.

it-support: Thanks — sounds like the corporate proxy is doing TLS interception which breaks pinning for certain SSO flows. For onboarding devices we expect no interception during enroll. Two immediate fixes: 1) try hotspot to finish setup (you already validated SSO works there), and 2) if you need to use corp Wi-Fi, we can push the proxy's subordinate cert to the machine via MDM so pin verification succeeds. Which do you prefer right now?

liam: I'll finish the SSO via hotspot so I can get to work. One follow-up: after I switched to hotspot, the MDM shows 'enrolled' but Okta shows device as 'untrusted'. It asks me to install the 'Okta Device Trust' profile but when I do it fails with 'system extension blocked' and there is no Allow button in Privacy & Security.

emily: New-hires aren't given admin by default. Want a temporary sudo to approve things?

liam: Yes please, that would speed things up.

emily: Granted 2h sudo for @liam.

liam: Reinstalled the Okta profile and now Privacy & Security shows the blocked message and an Allow button. Clicked Allow, rebooted. Post-reboot Okta still says 'device not trusted'. Error in Okta logs: 'attestation: missing hardware-backed key'.

it-support: 'missing hardware-backed key' often means the device didn't complete device attestation with our MDM server. Can you run and paste the output of: 

```bash
/usr/sbin/system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep "Hardware UUID"
```

and also `profiles show -type enrollment`?

liam: Hardware UUID: 7E5F1A2B-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-9C1D2E3F4A5B
profiles show output: Enrollment Profile: id=abc123, status=Enrolled, lastCheckin=2026-03-18T10:02:30Z

it-support: UUID looks good and enrollment shows Enrolled, so attestation should be possible. Two possible gaps: (A) Okta needs the Okta agent to register a key; (B) MDM-to-Okta attestation callback failed. @infra-oncall can you check the attestation relay logs for serial C02L1M2N3O4?

infra-oncall: Looking... attestation relay shows a 403 from Okta on the callback: "Client certificate required". Our relay attempted TLS to Okta without the client cert — config drift on the relay side. Pushing a fix to include the client cert used for Okta callbacks now.

liam: After a minute Okta updated to 'Device Trusted' — works now on hotspot and corp Wi-Fi (after restarting the browser). Thanks!

it-support: Nice. We'll follow up to ensure the relay certs are rotated in our runbook. One more: FileVault didn't prompt during setup. Should I enable manually?

liam: Enabled FileVault, it restarted and encryption started. `fdesetup status` says "FileVault is On".

macbot: [automated] FileVault personal recovery key escrowed to KMS for device C02L1M2N3O4.

liam: Quick question for docs: during setup the upgrade to macOS 14 wasn't offered. Is that intentional?

emily: Yes — we block major upgrades for 30 days after a new image is released to validate toolchain compatibility. Security patches still get pushed.

liam: Got it. Two tiny asks: 1) could we document that hotspot is a good isolation step for new hires? 2) add a note in the new-hire checklist to confirm Okta agent whitelist + Allow flow for macOS 13/14 so people don't miss the tiny privacy banner timing.

it-support: Great suggestions. We'll add both to the onboarding doc and note the relay cert fix. Welcome to Redwood, @liam — ping #new-hires if anything else crops up. :)
